  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "message": "This API key expired on 2026-09-01",
  "code": "API_KEY_EXPIRED",
  "hint": "Create a new key under API keys and use it instead.",
  "request_id": "4…
Every error answer also says what to do. hint is one plain sentence (chosen by code, else by status). fields lists the field keys the refusal is about, so a form can mark them. request_id matches the x-nivaro-request-id header and the API log; quote it when you report a problem. A key the route already set is never replaced, and error, message and code keep their values.
A write the database refuses is told in the collection’s field labels: a duplicate value names the field and your value ("Another record already has this PO number (4471)"), a missing link names the field you picked, a left-out required column answers REQUIRED_VALUE_MISSING, and a delete still linked to names the records that point at it. Constraint, table and column names never appear.
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity

{
  "error": "Supplier site is required",
  "code": "REQUIRED_VALUE_MISSING",
  "hint": "Fill in Supplier site, then save again.",
  "fields": ["supplier_site"],
  "request_id": "4f0c2a9e-…"
}

Code | Status | Meaning / NOT_SIGNED_IN | 401 | No credential was sent and there is no session. / TOKEN_INVALID | 401 | The bearer token matches no account. / ACCOUNT_NOT_ACTIVE | 401 | The credential is real. The account behind it is suspended. / API_KEY_INVALID | 401 | The API key matches none on file. / API_KEY_REVOKED | 401 | The API key is switched off. / API_KEY_EXPIRED | 401 | The API key passed its expiry date. The message names the date. / API_KEY_OWNER_INACTIVE | 401 | The account that owns the API key is not active. / API_KEY_IP_NOT_ALLOWED | 403 | The call came from outside the key's address allowlist. / API_KEY_SCOPE_MISSING | 403 | The key has no scope for the action on that collection. scope names both. / API_KEY_RATE_LIMITED | 429 | The key went past its calls-per-minute limit. Retry-After says how long to wait. / RATE_LIMITED | 429 | The caller went past the instance limit, when one is set. / MASQUERADE_EXPIRED | 401 | A view-as session ran out. / SIGN_IN_DISABLED | 401 | The account belongs to a role with sign-in turned off (the role's app access). Every session and token of that account is refused. / ADMIN_ONLY | 403 | The route is for administrators.

Code | Status | Meaning / LINKED_RECORD_MISSING | 422 | A field points at a record that does not exist. / RECORD_IN_USE | 409 | The record cannot be removed while other records point at it. / DUPLICATE_RECORD | 409 | A record with the same unique value already exists. / VALUE_TOO_LONG | 422 | A value is longer than its field allows. / REQUIRED_VALUE_MISSING | 422 | A field that must have a value was left out or sent empty. fields names it. / FIELD_NOT_FILTERABLE | 400 | A filter or sort names a calculated field that cannot be compared in the database. / VALIDATION_RULE_FAILED | 400 | A field rule refused the value. violations lists field, rule and message. / CHANGE_REASON_REQUIRED | 422 | The change needs _change_reason. violations lists the fields. / MIDAIR_COLLISION | 409 | Someone else changed the same fields. conflicts lists them. / DELETE_GUARDED | 409 | A deletion guard on the collection refused the delete. / DUPLICATE_ROW | 409 | A row of the same parent already holds these values. rule names the relation, fields the values compared, existing_id the row. / LINK_LIMIT_REACHED | 409 | The record already holds as many links of this kind as the relation allows. rule, max and current say which and how many. / PICKER_RULE_VIOLATED | 400 | The value is one the field's picker would not offer for this record (a field set to enforce its picker rules on every write). rule says which rule, field which field, parents the parent fields a cascade read. / RECORD_LOCKED | 409 | Another person holds the record's edit lock. The message names them. / EDIT_LOCKED | 403 | The record is in a step that only its creator, the step's owners and administrators may edit (the collection's summary-mode edit_lock rule). Child rows the rule lists are refused the same way.

blocks.h: Codes for reads and busy servers
blocks.t:
Code | Status | Meaning / UNKNOWN_FIELD | 400 | A filter, sort or field list names a field the collection does not have. fields lists them. / LIST_TIMEOUT | 503 | A list or search took too long and was stopped. Narrow it or try again. When only the count timed out, the rows still come back with meta.total_timed_out: true and no total. / SERVER_BUSY | 503 | No database connection came free in time (DB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_MS, default 10 s). Retry-After says when to try again. / DB_UNAVAILABLE | 503 | The database could not be reached: it refused or did not answer a new connection, or the server already knows it is away. Retry-After says when to try again. The request that failed was not sent to the database; a request that makes several changes may have saved an earlier one, so read the record again before repeating a write.
One list read returns at most 1000 rows, whatever limit asks for. The answer says so in meta.limit_capped and meta.applied_limit; page with offset (sort by a unique field such as id) to read more. GET /items/:collection/export pages for you, streamed to a temp file page by page: answered in the request it holds up to the request_rows export limit (50,000 unless an administrator changed it; x-nivaro-export-truncated names the limit when there were more), and stops when you disconnect; with background=auto or 1 a big export runs as a job holding every row (the file_rows limit, none by default — see Data Export).
A refusal from the database names the constraint that refused the write. It never includes the statement or the database name. Administrators read every refused credential under Monitoring, Integrations, Inbound, in the Refused credentials list.

Static tokens let scripts, server-side processes, and the SDK authenticate without a browser session. Each user can have one token at a time. Generating a new token immediately invalidates the previous one.
Method | Path | Auth | Description / POST | /api/users/me/token | Any authenticated user | Generate a token for yourself. / DELETE | /api/users/me/token | Any authenticated user | Revoke your token. / POST | /api/users/:id/token | Admin | Generate a token for another user. / DELETE | /api/users/:id/token | Admin | Revoke another user's token.

POST /api/users/me/token
→ 200 { "data": { "token": "3a7f2b9c1d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c..." } }

DELETE /api/users/me/token
→ 204 No Content
Tokens are returned only once — on generation. Store them securely. The token value is not readable again after the response is closed; only a hash indicator is stored.

Nivaro auto-generates an OpenAPI 3.1 specification from the live nivaro_collections + nivaro_fields metadata. The spec is always current — it is re-built on every request, so adding a new collection shows up immediately without a restart.
Endpoint | Description / GET /api/schema.json | OpenAPI 3.1 spec as JSON. Safe to consume from CI, code generators, Postman, etc. / GET /api/schema | Swagger UI explorer — interactive, try-it-out enabled, Bearer auth persisted.
The spec includes a component schema for every non-hidden collection, a list-response wrapper with data, total, limit, and offset, and full path definitions for GET list, GET by ID, POST, PATCH, and DELETE.
The spec references two security schemes: bearerToken (static token) and sessionCookie. In Swagger UI, click Authorize and paste your static token to make authenticated requests directly from the browser.

The generic items API works against any table registered in nivaro_collections. All requests require authentication and pass through the RBAC permission layer.
Method | Path | Description / GET | /api/items/:collection | List records. Supports filter, sort, fields, limit, offset, search. / GET | /api/items/:collection/:id | Single record by primary key. / GET | /api/items/:collection/aggregate | Counts, sums and averages over the rows a list read would match, optionally grouped. / any | /items/:collection[/:id] | The same routes at the host root, for callers written against the legacy base URL. Answered by the /api handler: one request-log row, same authentication, same body and query string. / POST | /api/items/:collection | Create a record. / PATCH | /api/items/:collection/:id | Update a record (partial). / DELETE | /api/items/:collection/:id | Delete a record.

Param | Default | Description / fields | * (all allowed) | Comma-separated field names: id,name,created_at / filter | none | JSON filter object — see Filter DSL below. / sort | none | Comma-separated. Prefix - for descending: -created_at,name / limit | 25 | Max rows (hard cap 1000). / offset | 0 | Row offset for pagination. / page | 1 | Shorthand for offset. page=2&limit=25 → offset=25. / after | none | Keyset paging. start for the first page, then the next_cursor of the page before. Replaces offset and page. / count | 1 | When 0, the count query is skipped and total answers null. When approx, a total counted in the last 30 seconds by the same query may answer instead, and total_approx: true says so. The rows are always read fresh. An unfiltered list reads the row count SQL Server keeps for the table. When the caller’s access rules look at another table (teams, owners, scopes), the first page always counts live, and only that caller’s own cursor pages (after=) may reuse its total. / labels | 0 | When 1 on an id _in lookup (a list resolving the labels of linked records), rows read in the last 30 seconds by the same query may answer without a database read. A write to the collection through the API clears them at once; a write by a stored procedure or script shows when they expire. Ignored for any other filter, and when the caller’s access rules look at another table. / search | none | Every word must appear in one of the string/text fields (contains match). A collection can name the columns searched in Table Editor → Settings → Collection Browser → Search columns (browser_config.search_fields); leaving long notes out keeps search fast on big tables. A collection can also let each word match a related record’s label: browser_config.search_relations lists relation paths ending in a text field (["regions.name", "division.region.name"]; M2O and M2M hops, at most 3, up to 10 paths), so a project is found by its region’s name. No system table is reached, with one exception: a to-one link to a person may end on their first or last name (["contact.first_name", "contact.last_name"]), so a record is found by a person on it — never by any other column of the user table. Each hop is judged as the caller — the link and the field must be readable to them, and their row filters and User Scopes apply on every hop — and a path they cannot read is skipped. Off when the request sends its own search_fields. / search_fields | none | Comma list narrowing search to these string/text fields for this request, e.g. search=ppc&search_fields=cifa_number,description. Only ever narrows (on top of the collection’s own list); unknown names are ignored, and a list matching none searches as without it. Catalog pickers search what their rows show first this way. / search_rank | 0 | With search, search_rank=1 orders the matches by how well they match the searched columns before the request’s own sort: the first search_fields column equal to the text, another column equal to it, the first column starting with it, another starting with it, every word starting a word of some column, then the rest. Only the order changes — which rows match stays the search, and only the readable columns the search reads are compared. Ignored with keyset paging (after). Catalog pickers rank their search this way. / picker | 0 | When 1, applies picker filters and exclusions; used by relation pickers. / typo | 0 | With picker=1 and search: when the first page finds nothing, the same typo pass global search uses runs over the picker’s display fields (from fields, else the display template; at most two text fields; people pickers name and email only), and its matches are read again as you with the same filter, User Scopes and picker exclusions. Rows come back best first with fuzzy: true and meta.fuzzy: true (“Kristna” finds Kristina). Searches under four letters, ids and tables over 200,000 rows never get it; the pass has its own 1.2 s budget. / translate | 0 | When 1, includes _translations map for each translatable field.

A field list may name a to-many relation and the fields wanted from it: fields=id,lines.amount,tags.name. Each record on the page answers with a list under that name. The related rows are read as the caller, so the permissions, field list, row filter and scopes of the related collection apply. A caller who may not read the related collection gets empty lists.
GET /api/items/orders?limit=2&fields=id,number,lines.amount,lines.line_number,tags.name

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 41,
      "number": "SO-1041",
      "lines": [
        { "id": 900, "order": 41, "amount": 120, "line_number": 1 },
  …
A record lists 200 related rows per relation at most. When a list was cut, the response names the relation in truncated_relations. Related rows nest two levels deep. One read per relation per page is made, never one per record.
A field name the collection does not have answers 400 with code UNKNOWN_FIELD and the names in fields.

A relation whose links point at different collections row by row (a contact that is either a person or an outside email address) answers one entry per link: the link id, the collection it names, the linked id, and the linked record under item. fields=contacts.* or contacts.item.* reads the whole linked record; contacts.item.email (or the shorthand contacts.email) reads only the fields named; asking only for contacts.id,contacts.collection skips the linked record. People answer what the person directory (GET /users) shows and nothing more: the directory fields, never a suspended, redacted or placeholder account, and nothing at all through an API key whose scopes leave out nivaro_users. Every other collection is read as the caller, and a record the caller may not read, or a collection the relation does not allow, answers item: null. A relation left out of the field list the caller may read answers nothing. One read per linked collection per page, never one per link. The same works on a single record and through a relation (request.contacts.*).
GET /api/items/requests/32842?fields=id,contacts.item.email

{
  "data": {
    "id": 32842,
    "contacts": [
      { "id": 52295, "collection": "directus_users", "item_id": "7A0411F3-…", "item": { "id": "7A0411F3-…", "email": "pat@example.…

POST /api/items/batch-read carries up to 20 reads. Each is a list read (no id) or a single-record read, with the query keys the GET routes take (fields, filter, sort, limit, offset, page, search, after, count, conditions) as strings or structured values. Every read runs as the caller exactly as its own GET would and answers its own status — a forbidden collection is 403, a missing record 404, a bad filter 400 — so one refused read never fails the others. A list read answers its rows in data and its paging facts in meta. Writes never batch. SDK: readMany([...]); a host can let NivaroProvider batchReads gather the record reads its components fire in the same moment into one batch.
POST /api/items/batch-read
{ "reads": [
  { "key": "regions", "collection": "regions", "query": { "fields": "id,short_name", "limit": 5 } },
  { "key": "order", "collection": "orders", "id": 41, "query": { "fields": "id,number" } },
  { "ke…

blocks.h: Several small GETs in one request

blocks.t:
Offset paging pays for every row it skips, and rows written during the walk shift the pages. A cursor names the last row of the page just read, so the next page costs the same however far the walk is, and a write elsewhere moves nothing. Send after=start for the first page and the next_cursor of each page for the next. next_cursor is null on the last page. The collection browser and queue worklists page forward this way on their own, and ask by page number for a page they have no cursor for (the last page, a jump). GET /api/queues/:id/items takes after beside page too: a materialized queue in its default order or sorted by label, state, collection or at-risk reads the page by cursor and answers next_cursor; any other queue or sort pages by number and answers none. When a total is approximate the collection browser reads "of about 85,603 records".
GET /api/items/orders?limit=500&sort=-amount&fields=id,amount&after=start&count=0

{
  "data": [{ "id": 307072, "amount": 249387248 }, ...],
  "total": null,
  "limit": 500,
  "offset": 0,
  "next_cursor": "eyJjIjoib3JkZXJzIiwicyI6Ii1hbW91b…
Rule | Detail / Sort | By the record's own stored fields. id is added as the tie-break, so no two rows tie. / Same request | Keep sort, filter and search the same for the whole walk. The cursor is signed for one collection and one sort. / CURSOR_SORT_UNSUPPORTED | The sort names a linked record or a calculated field that is not stored. / CURSOR_MISMATCH | The cursor was made for another collection or another sort. / CURSOR_INVALID | The cursor was changed or cut.

GET /api/items/:collection/aggregate answers figures over the rows a list read with the same filter and search would match for the caller. It never counts a row the caller could not list.
Param | Description / groupBy | Up to 4 stored fields, comma-separated. Without it, one row for the whole set. / countAll | When 1, the number of rows in each group. / count | Fields: rows that hold a value. / countDistinct | Fields: different values. / sum, avg | Number fields. / min, max | Number, date and short text fields. / sort | Group fields, countAll, or <function>.<field>. Prefix - for descending. / limit, offset | Groups per page. Default 100, 1000 at most.
GET /api/items/orders/aggregate?groupBy=status&sum=amount&countAll=1&sort=-sum.amount
    &filter={"created_at":{"_gte":"2026-01-01"}}

{
  "data": [
    { "group": { "status": "open" }, "countAll": 329, "sum": { "amount": 33592071.85 } },
…
Refusals answer 400 with a code: AGGREGATE_FIELD_INVALID (a sum over text, a field that is not stored), AGGREGATE_TOO_WIDE (more than 4 group fields or 24 figures), AGGREGATE_SORT_INVALID (a sort that is not part of the request).

blocks.h: Move to a pipeline step on an update ($state)

blocks.t:
PATCH /api/items/:collection/:id?dry_run=1 reports what the update would change and saves nothing. Everything a real update runs before it writes runs here: contracts, permissions, row filters and User Scopes, the edit lock, mid-air collisions (_base_revision), before-hooks (with ctx.dryRun = true), change-reason rules, rules, field rules, row rules, computed fields, validation, relation limits and picker rules. The UPDATE is tried inside a transaction that is rolled back, so the database’s own refusals are found too. No activity row, revision, after-hook, notification, webhook, rollup or live update happens.
PATCH /api/items/orders/1042?dry_run=1
{ "status": "approved", "colour": "red" }

// Response (200)
{
  "dry_run": true,
  "ok": true,
  "status": 200,
  "would": "update",
  "id": "1042",
  "changes": [
    { "field": "status", "from": "re…
from and to are the values as you read them. A record you may not update, one outside your scope, and a collection that does not exist answer a real 403 / 404, as an update would. A sandbox key may preview too.

GET /api/items/:collection/filter-check?filter=<json> judges a filter without reading a record. Each clause of the filter is run on its own through the same checks a list read runs (fields, relation paths, operators, field read access), so every problem is named, not just the first. Clauses that pass are also checked against the field: a text operator on a number or date, a range on a yes/no field or an id, a value a number or date column can never match, and a value outside the field’s choices (a choice label where the stored value was meant). Where the fix is clear (the nearest field name, the operator as the API spells it, the stored choice value, a single value wrapped in a list), suggestion is the corrected filter. It is only offered when it passes every check itself.
GET /api/items/orders/filter-check?filter={"stauts":{"_eq":"Open"},"amount":{"_like":"5"}}

{ "data": {
  "ok": false,
  "collection": "orders",
  "errors": [
    { "path": "stauts", "code": "UNKNOWN_FIELD", "message": "orders has no field …

GET /api/changes is a change feed for a client that cannot keep a live connection (a script, a nightly sync, an MCP assistant). Call it once without a cursor to start from now (or with since=<ISO time>), keep the cursor it returns, and pass it next time. It lists record ids, the action (create, update, delete) and the names of the fields that changed, never values and never who changed them. Read the records for their values. Only records you can see now are listed, and field names are cut to the fields you can read. A delete is listed when you deleted it yourself, or when you can see every record of that collection (otherwise a deleted id could not be checked against your scope). Collections whose audit level keeps no activity never appear. has_more: true means call again at once; the newest few seconds wait for the next call.
GET /api/changes?cursor=c1.eyJhIjo5MTIzNH0&collections=orders,order_lines&limit=100

{ "data": {
  "changes": [
    { "collection": "orders", "id": "1042", "action": "update", "fields": ["status", "approved_on"], "at": "2026-10-29T14:02:11.…
Parameter | Meaning / cursor | The cursor the last call returned. A cursor this feed did not make is a 400 BAD_CURSOR. / since | Without a cursor: start at this time. / collections | Comma list (up to 50). Ones you cannot read come back in not_readable. / limit | Records per page, 1–500 (default 100). A record changed several times in one page is listed once.

A many-to-many relation takes its links under the relation's field name, on create and on update. Plain arrays add links and never remove one. { "delete": [ids] } removes links, { "set": [ids] } makes the record's links exactly the ids listed. Links are written through the junction collection as the caller, so its permissions, history and any limit apply.
PATCH /api/items/articles/9
{ "tags": [3, 4] }                    // adds 3 and 4
{ "tags": { "delete": [3] } }         // removes 3
{ "tags": { "set": [4, 5] } }         // the article is tagged 4 and 5, nothing else

// a polymorphic link…
A polymorphic link (a relation that allows several collections) stores the collection beside the id. An entry that is a bare id takes the collection the record form would write: directus_users when the relation allows it, else the first allowed collection. A modern name is stored under its legacy spelling when only that is allowed.

Send an Idempotency-Key header with any POST, PATCH or DELETE under /api/items, /api/comments or /api/tasks, with a pipeline or workflow move (POST /api/pipelines/instance/:collection/:item/transition, POST /api/workflows/instance/:id/transition) or with a GraphQL mutation. The first request runs. A repeat of the same request under the same key within 24 hours returns the first answer and writes nothing, with the header Idempotent-Replay: true. Use a fresh unique value per logical write, such as a UUID, and reuse it only when retrying that write.
POST /api/items/orders
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: 5f0c1d5e-7d0a-4c59-9a40-1d6c1c0f2a11
Content-Type: application/json

{ "customer": 42, "total": 159 }
Situation | Answer / Same key, same request, first one finished | The first answer again, Idempotent-Replay: true. / Same key, same request, first one still running | 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After. / Same key, different path or body | 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. / The first request failed | The key is released. The retry runs as a new request. / Key longer than 200 characters or containing spaces | 400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID. / A key minted by a Nivaro app (nvr-…) whose first try failed with a server error | That error again: an automatic retry never runs a write that may have partly landed. A refusal (4xx) or a 503 SERVER_BUSY / DB_UNAVAILABLE releases the key. / Same key with a different query string | 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (the query string is part of the request). / A delete repeated under the same key | The first answer (204) again, not a 404 for the record it already removed.
The admin and the record apps use this to ride out a deploy or restart: a record create, update or delete, a pipeline move, or a comment or task write whose answer was lost is retried with the same key for up to two minutes, so it happens once. Other writes (bulk actions, uploads, partner pushes) are never retried automatically.
Keys belong to the caller that sent them. Two API keys, or two users, may use the same value without meeting each other. IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS changes how long answers are kept.

blocks.h: When a create matches an existing record

blocks.t:
Status | Scenario / 400 | Invalid filter syntax, bad request body, invalid field names. / 401 | Missing or invalid authentication. / 403 | Authenticated but lacks permission (collection/field/action). / 404 | Record not found (single read/update/delete). / 409 | Conflict — concurrent update, item locked, or relation constraint violated. / 422 | Validation rule violation or hard-block AI rule triggered.
Relations (M2O FK, M2M, O2M) are resolved automatically in single-record reads. In list responses, M2O relations are included as nested objects; O2M and M2M are not included (use relation option endpoints to fetch related records separately).
Filters are URL-encoded JSON objects. The key is the field name, the value is an object with an operator and value. Supports scalar operators, logical combinators, and relation traversal.

Key | Values | Keeps / $addendums | active, none, any | Records with an addendum in flight, with none in flight, or that ever had one. / $at_risk | a rule id, a list of ids, or "any" | Records that match one of the named highlight rules. / $integrations | danger, warning, positive, none | Records by how they stand with their integration partners.
These keys work in filter, inside _and and _or, and as paths in conditions. GraphQL spells them _state, _origin, _addendums, _at_risk and _integrations.

A filter is checked before it runs. A part that cannot be compiled is refused with 400 and a code. It is never dropped, because a dropped part answers more rows than were asked for.
Code | Meaning / FILTER_OPERATOR_UNKNOWN | The operator does not exist. operator names it, path says where. / FILTER_PATH_UNSUPPORTED | A nested key under a field that links to no other record. / FILTER_VALUE_INVALID | _in and _nin take a list, _between takes two values, _and and _or take a list of filters. / FILTER_TOO_DEEP | More than 8 levels of nesting. / UNKNOWN_FIELD | The collection has no such field. fields names it. / FIELD_NOT_FILTERABLE | A calculated field that cannot be expressed in SQL.

All endpoints require admin access. The Collections API manages the nivaro_collections and nivaro_fields metadata registry.
Method | Path | Description / GET | /api/collections | List all registered collections with field counts. / GET | /api/collections/:name | Single collection metadata + its fields array. / GET | /api/collections?names=a,b,c | Batched metadata: up to 50 table-shaped names → { data: { <name>: <same body as GET /:name> }, missing: [names not registered], errors: { <name>: message } }. 400 on a bad name or too many. The shared client batches GET /collections/:name reads made within ~10 ms through it automatically. / POST | /api/collections | Register a new collection from existing table. / PATCH | /api/collections/:name | Update collection settings (label, icon, etc). / DELETE | /api/collections/:name | Unregister collection from the CMS (table is not dropped). / GET | /api/collections/:name/fields | List all fields for a collection. / POST | /api/collections/:name/fields | Register a field from existing column. / PATCH | /api/collections/:name/fields/:field | Update field metadata (label, interface, etc). / DELETE | /api/collections/:name/fields/:field | Unregister a field (column is not dropped).

User management endpoints. List users, view profiles, manage roles, and handle delegation.
Method | Path | Auth required / GET | /api/users | Admin — list all users with pagination. / GET | /api/users/:id | Any user (own record) or admin. / POST | /api/users | Admin — create a user (email required). / PATCH | /api/users/:id | Own record or admin. Admins can change role/status. / DELETE | /api/users/:id | Admin — cannot delete yourself. / POST | /api/users/me/token | Any authenticated user — generate own static token. / DELETE | /api/users/me/token | Any authenticated user — revoke own static token. / POST | /api/users/:id/token | Admin — generate token for another user. / DELETE | /api/users/:id/token | Admin — revoke another user's token. / POST | /api/users/me/delegate | Any authenticated user — set own delegation.
Use me as the ID to target the currently-authenticated user. Token endpoints are also covered in the Static Tokens section above.
Filtering the list (administrators): filter=<JSON> or the bracket form filter[role][_eq]=<id>, filter[status]=suspended (no operator = _eq), filter[last_name][_in]=Kelly,Kanniappan — both forms together must both hold. Operators _eq, _neq, _in, _nin on the people columns. Anything the list cannot apply — malformed JSON or bracket keys, an unknown or withheld column, another operator, _or — is a 400 INVALID_FILTER that says why, never the whole list as if filtered. The people directory non-administrators read narrows by search= only; a filter there is a 400. Suspended people appear only with include_suspended=true.

GET /api/users?limit=10&offset=0
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>

// Response (200)
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "user-1",
      "email": "jane@example.com",
      "first_name": "Jane",
      "last_name": "Smith",
      "role": "edit…

Users can delegate their ownership to another user when out of office. Delegated users inherit all ownership responsibilities.
Field | Type | Notes / manager_id | uuid | null | Direct manager (admin-only). / delegate_id | uuid | null | User who receives delegation while out of office. / delegate_expires_at | datetime | null | When delegation expires; null = indefinite. / is_out_of_office | boolean | Master switch — delegation active only when true.

Manage roles and their permissions. Roles control what actions users can perform on which collections and fields.
Method | Path | Description / GET | /api/roles | List all roles with policy counts. / GET | /api/roles/:id | Single role + its complete policies array. / POST | /api/roles | Create a new role. / PATCH | /api/roles/:id | Update role name, description, or admin_access flag. / DELETE | /api/roles/:id | Delete role (blocked if users are assigned to it). / GET | /api/roles/:id/policies | List all policies for a role. / POST | /api/roles/:id/policies | Add a policy: { collection, action, fields? }. / DELETE | /api/roles/policies/:policyId | Delete a specific policy.
All endpoints under /api/workflows. Admin auth required unless noted.

Manage flows — automated workflows with triggers and operations.
Method | Path | Description / GET | /api/flows | List flows with operation counts and next_run for scheduled flows. / GET | /api/flows/:id | Single flow with parsed operations array. / POST | /api/flows | Create a new flow. / PATCH | /api/flows/:id | Update flow — automatically resyncs cron if trigger/status changed. / DELETE | /api/flows/:id | Delete flow and cascade-remove all operations. / POST | /api/flows/:id/trigger | Manually trigger an active flow immediately. / POST | /api/flows/:id/operations | Add an operation to a flow. / PATCH | /api/flows/:id/operations/:opId | Update an operation. / DELETE | /api/flows/:id/operations/:opId | Delete an operation. / GET | /api/flows/registered-operations | List available operation types (built-in + extension-registered). / GET | /api/flows/registered-triggers | List available trigger types (built-in + extension-registered).

POST /api/flows/flow-1/operations
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "log",
  "name": "Log start",
  "options": { "message": "Digest started", "level": "info" },
  "sort": 0
}

// Response (201)
…

Type | Description | Options / schedule | Cron-scheduled recurring job | { "cron": "0 9 * * *" } / manual | Triggered by POST /flows/:id/trigger | N/A / event | Custom extension-registered event | Varies by event / webhook | Incoming HTTP request | URL pattern

Type | Description / log | Write to server log / mail | Send email via SMTP / webhook | Make outbound HTTP request / notification | Create in-app notification / external-api | Call configured external API / condition | Branch logic / transform | Map/set/delete fields / <custom> | Extension-registered operation type
All endpoints under /api/pipelines. Admin auth required unless noted.
All external API routes require admin access (role.admin_access = true). Secrets are masked on GET — re-submit the masked value to leave a secret unchanged.

Method | Path | Description / GET | /api/external-apis | List all configs. Secrets masked. / POST | /api/external-apis | Create config. Body: name, base_url, auth_type, auth_config, headers, enabled. / GET | /api/external-apis/:id | Single config. Secrets masked. / PATCH | /api/external-apis/:id | Update config. Masked secret values preserved. / DELETE | /api/external-apis/:id | Delete config and all its endpoint templates.

auth_type | auth_config fields / none | {} / bearer | { token } / api_key | { key, value, in: "header"|"query", param_name } / basic | { username, password } / oauth2_cc | { client_id, client_secret, token_url, scope? }

Both call routes require authentication but not admin access. Auth credentials stay server-side.
Method | Path | Description / POST | /api/external-apis/:id/call | Call any arbitrary endpoint on the API. Body: method?, path?, body?, query?, headers?. / POST | /api/external-apis/endpoints/:slugOrId/call | Call a pre-defined endpoint template by numeric id or slug. Caller overrides merge on top of saved defaults.

Method | Path | Description / GET | /api/external-apis/:id/endpoints | List all endpoint templates for an API. / POST | /api/external-apis/:id/endpoints | Create an endpoint template. Body: name, slug?, method, path, description?, default_body?, default_query?, default_headers?, sort?. / PATCH | /api/external-apis/endpoints/:eid | Update an endpoint template. / DELETE | /api/external-apis/endpoints/:eid | Delete an endpoint template. / PATCH | /api/external-apis/:id/endpoints/reorder | Bulk reorder. Body: [{ id, sort }].

Field | Type | Description / id | number | Auto-increment primary key. / api_id | number | FK → nivaro_external_apis.id (CASCADE on delete). / name | string | Human-readable name shown in the test panel. / slug | string | null | Optional URL-safe identifier. Nivaro auto-generates a GraphQL schema from the live nivaro_collections + nivaro_fields metadata — the same source used to build the OpenAPI spec. Every non-hidden collection gets query and mutation fields automatically. Schema is rebuilt in the onReady hook when the server starts, and can be manually rebuilt at runtime.
Endpoint | Description / GET /api/graphql | Redirects a browser to the admin app's bundled GraphiQL explorer (/graphql). Administrators can run it as any named API key (Security → API keys → Run the playground as a key). / POST /api/graphql | GraphQL endpoint. Body: { query, variables?, operationName? }. / POST /api/graphql/rebuild | Admin — rebuild the schema from current nivaro_collections/fields.
GraphQL queries and mutations go through the same RBAC permission layer as the REST API. Unauthenticated requests receive UNAUTHENTICATED errors; forbidden operations receive FORBIDDEN errors.

A query is measured before it executes. The total number of selected fields is capped at GRAPHQL_MAX_SELECTIONS (default 2500). Nesting depth is unlimited by default — set GRAPHQL_MAX_DEPTH on the instance to cap it, or give a named API key its own graphql_max_depth, which applies only to that key. A refused query answers HTTP 400 with an errors[] message naming the measured cost and the limit.

Every GraphQL request logs the operation it ran (its name, else the first root field), its kind, the measured depth and selection count, how many errors the answer carried, and which @deprecated fields it selected. Monitoring → API Analytics → GraphQL by operation shows each operation's calls, p50/p95 latency, error rate, average cost, top callers and slowest calls (GET /api/api-analytics/graphql?hours=); a strip above it names every deprecated field still being selected and by whom — what to check before the deprecation window closes.

For each non-hidden collection with at least one visible field, the schema includes:
• An object type named after the collection (e.g. articles) • A page-facts type named collectionName_metadata with total, limit, and offset • Three query fields: collectionName (list of items), collectionName_metadata (page facts for the same arguments) and collectionName_by_id (single) • Three mutation fields: create_collectionName, update_collectionName_item, delete_collectionName_item • A typed filter input type named collectionName_filter with per-field operator inputs and _and/_or combinators

blocks.h: Links that may point at several collections

blocks.t: A nested field is read with the caller's own access to the related collection. Read permission, row filters, user scopes and the policy's field list all apply, exactly as they do when the related collection is queried on its own. A to-many field returns only the rows the caller may read; a to-one field returns null when the caller may not read the related record. API keys that carry scope restrictions are narrowed the same way, whoever owns them.

Nivaro field type | GraphQL type / string, text, uuid, hash, csv | String / integer, bigInteger | Int / float, decimal | Float / boolean | Boolean / datetime, date, time | String (ISO 8601) / json | JSON (custom scalar — any value) / id field (any type) | ID

Argument | Type | Description / filter | JSON | Filter DSL object — same operators as REST (e.g. { status: { _eq: "active" } }) / sort | [String] | Array of sort fields. Prefix with - for descending. / limit | Int | Max items (server default: 25, max: 1000). / offset | Int | Row offset for pagination. / search | String | Fulltext search across string/text fields. / after | String | Keyset paging: "start" for the first page, then the next_cursor of the page before. Replaces offset.

blocks.h: Nested lists take the list arguments
blocks.t: A to-many field inside a record takes filter, sort, limit and offset of its own. The rows are the ones the caller may read in the related collection.

<collection>_aggregated(filter, search, groupBy, sort, limit, offset) answers counts, sums and averages over the rows the same filter would list for the caller. Which figures are computed is read from the selection, so a query pays for what it asks.
query {
  # one row for the whole set
  orders_aggregated(filter: { status: { _eq: "open" } }) {
    countAll
    sum { amount }
    avg { amount }
    count { vendor }
  }

  # one row per group, largest first
  byType: orders_aggregated(g…
group is a JSON object of the group-by values. sum and avg list number fields; min and max list number, date and short text fields; count and countDistinct list every stored field. Up to 4 group fields and 1000 groups per page. A refusal carries extensions.code (AGGREGATE_FIELD_INVALID, AGGREGATE_TOO_WIDE, AGGREGATE_SORT_INVALID).
Every collection gets a generated collectionName_filter input type with typed operator inputs per field — no raw JSON required. The filter arg is fully type-safe in GraphiQL autocomplete.

blocks.h: Reading record states from an integration

blocks.t: Every collection has three mutation fields: create, update, and delete. They follow the same naming pattern as query fields.

Mutations return the full record as it was after the operation. Request any fields you need — the operation executes regardless. Validation errors return 400 with details.
Mutation | Arguments | Auth / create_collectionName | data: JSON (all fields optional) | User with create permission / create_collectionName_item | data: JSON — Directus-compatible alias | User with create permission / create_collectionName_items | data: [JSON] — batch, one row per entry; all or nothing, and its webhooks / flows / notifications wait for the whole batch and are dropped when it is undone | User with create permission / update_collectionName_item | id: ID!, data: JSON (partial), state: String — move to this pipeline step (or data._state), state_comment: String | User with update permission; the move as a manual transition / update_collectionName_items | ids: [ID!]!, data: JSON — the same change to several records; state, state_comment | User with update permission / update_collectionName_batch | data: [JSON] — each entry is { id, …fields } | User with update permission / delete_collectionName_item | id: ID! | User with delete permission / delete_collectionName_items | ids: [ID!]! — batch, returns { ids } | User with delete permission
Create/update payloads accept Directus-era relation shapes: an M2O may be { id: … }, and an M2M alias may be a single object, an array of { junction_field: { id } } entries, or { create: [...] } — alias writes are additive (junction rows are created, never detached).

blocks.h: Changing several records in one call
blocks.t:
mutation {
  # the same change to each
  update_orders_items(ids: [11, 12, 13], data: { status: "approved" }) { id status }

  # a different change per record
  update_orders_batch(data: [
    { id: 11, total: 120 },
    { id: 12, total: 80…
• Each record is changed as the caller, one after the other, with the same rules as a single update. • All or nothing. When one record is refused, the records changed before it get their earlier values back and the error says so. • At most 500 records per call.
An update can also move the record to a pipeline step: update_<collection>_item(id, data, state: "canceled"), or data: { _state: "canceled" }. The move runs as a person's transition with every permission, and a refused move refuses the whole update. See Pipeline Engine → Move by Step on Update.
Every GraphQL transition (execute_workflow_transition, execute_pipeline_transition, workflow_transition) runs the same move as the record page and REST: required roles, admin-only and extension checks, owner-only (and creator) moves, required notes, requirements, conditions and the edit lock, then the transition actions, history, notifications and the activity row. A refusal is an error with the REST status and code in extensions (for example TRANSITION_OWNER_REQUIRED, TRANSITION_COMMENT_REQUIRED, RECORD_LOCKED).

blocks.h: Changes for existing callers of the transition mutations (2026-11)
blocks.t:
• execute_workflow_transition, execute_pipeline_transition and workflow_transition now refuse what the record page refuses: owner-only moves for non-owners (unless the move is open by its rule), unmet conditions, extension checks, a missing required note, someone else editing the record (RECORD_LOCKED), a move already running. • The transition's actions now run for all three (partner pushes, emails, field writes set on the move), and the activity row and history are written as for a person's move. • newState / the instance answered is where the record came to rest after the automatic moves that follow, not the move's own target. • A completed record can move through an escape-hatch transition authored out of its final step (Uncancel), as on the record page. • Sending the same move twice quickly answers the second with 409 TRANSITION_DUPLICATE. • When an automatic move that follows is marked to run in the background, the answer comes back while that chain is still running.
Moving by step on an update (state, data._state) does not answer a requirements review or move a record someone else is editing: use the record page or the transition route for those.

blocks.h: When a create matches an existing record
Create a record with its related rows

blocks.t: Send an Idempotency-Key header with a mutation request. A repeat of the same request under the same key returns the first answer and writes nothing. A mutation that answered with errors releases its key, so the retry runs again. Queries are never deduplicated. See Items API → Safe retries with Idempotency-Key for the full rules.

Subscription | Arguments | Fires when / workflowStateChanged | collection, item | A workflow instance transitions to a new state. / pipelineStateChanged | collection, item | A pipeline instance transitions to a new state. / itemMutated | collection, item, fields, actions | A record is created, updated or deleted. fields narrows to updates that changed one of the named fields; actions narrows to create, update or delete.

Pass a static token via connectionParams.authorization, or a one-shot ticket via connectionParams.ticket. A ticket comes from GET /api/events/ticket, called with any sign-in the HTTP API accepts (session cookie, static token, View-as, or a named API key — whose scopes, row restrictions and depth cap then apply to the connection). A ticket works once and expires after 60 seconds.
A connection stays tied to what signed it in. When that sign-in ends — logout, a revoked session or API key, a rotated token, or an account that is no longer active — the connection closes with code 4401 within 30 seconds.
The GraphiQL explorer (admin /graphql, which GET /api/graphql redirects to) does not support subscriptions (HTTP-only). Use a WebSocket-capable client such as graphql-ws, the SSE endpoint below, or a tool like Altair GraphQL Client.

For clients whose proxies block WebSockets, every subscription (and every live query) is also served over Server-Sent Events at /api/graphql/stream. It uses the graphql-sse "distinct connections" shape: one operation per stream, each result as event: next with the execution result as data, then event: complete. A plain query answers once and completes. Mutations are refused with 405 — send them to POST /api/graphql.
// fetch-based clients (headers allowed): POST with the usual body
POST /api/graphql/stream
Authorization: Bearer nvk_…
Accept: text/event-stream
{ "query": "subscription { itemMutated(collection: "orders") { item action changed_fields } }"…
• Authentication is the HTTP API's own: session cookie, Bearer static token, View-as, or a named API key with its scopes and row restrictions. EventSource cannot send headers, so it uses ?ticket= (one-shot, 60 seconds). A long-lived credential never goes in the URL. • The same filters and per-subscriber checks as WebSocket apply: the collection read gate, fields / actions narrowing, and workflow / pipeline events built for each subscriber. • A comment heartbeat goes out every 25 seconds (GRAPHQL_SSE_HEARTBEAT_MS), and each heartbeat re-checks the sign-in. When it has ended, the stream sends a result with error code SESSION_ENDED, then complete. • Resume: itemMutated events carry their event-journal position as the SSE id. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID (EventSource does this by itself) to get the events you missed, replayed through the same filters. When the journal no longer reaches back that far (about 24 hours), the stream sends event: reset — refetch what you show. Workflow and pipeline subscriptions resume live only. • Query variables in a GET URL end up in request logs. Use POST for variables that carry anything sensitive.

GraphQL requests authenticate the same way as REST requests — session cookie or static token Bearer header. Unauthenticated requests are allowed to reach the endpoint but all resolvers return UNAUTHENTICATED errors, and schema introspection (__schema, __type) is refused. A graphql-ws connection that signs nothing in is closed with 4403. Nested lists are capped per request: GRAPHQL_MAX_NESTED_QUERIES (default 25,000 nested reads) and GRAPHQL_MAX_NESTED_ROWS (default 250,000 nested rows), 0 = off; past either the request answers QUERY_TOO_COSTLY. A nested filter or sort may name only fields the caller can read, and never a credential.

Open GET /api/graphql in a browser — it redirects to the admin app's GraphiQL explorer at /graphql. If you are already logged in to the admin UI your session cookie is sent automatically. To use a static token instead, open the Headers panel at the bottom of GraphiQL and add:
{ "Authorization": "Bearer 3a7f2b9c1d4e..." }

When you register a new collection or field via the Collections API, the GraphQL schema is not automatically updated — it was built at server startup. Call the rebuild endpoint to pick up the changes without restarting.
POST /api/graphql/rebuild
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>

→ 200 { "ok": true, "types": 42 }

• After registering a new collection via POST /api/collections • After adding a new field via POST /api/collections/:name/fields • After registering a new relation that affects type generation • After hiding/unhiding a collection or field that affects schema visibility
Rebuild is admin-only. It is safe to call at any time — in-flight GraphQL requests use the old schema until they complete; new requests after the rebuild use the updated schema.

Every rebuild that changes the schema writes a line-level diff (+ type, - workflows.old_field) to the changelog, GET /api/graphql/changelog (admin), and a removal notifies administrators. A field is retired in two steps: mark it deprecated in the Table Editor (Behavior → Deprecated for API callers, with a note naming the replacement) — the schema then carries @deprecated(reason: …) and clients that introspect see it — and remove it once the policy window has passed. Removing a served field before then is refused with 409 FIELD_NOT_DEPRECATED or FIELD_DEPRECATION_TOO_RECENT, naming the date it becomes removable; an administrator may force it with ?force=1, which the activity log records. The window is Settings → Content → API field deprecation window: blank = 14 days, 0 = no policy.
The @nivaro/sdk package is a fully-typed TypeScript client for the Nivaro REST, GraphQL, and realtime APIs. Works in Node.js, browsers, and edge runtimes.
pnpm add @nivaro/sdk

blocks.h: MCP server (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor)
blocks.t:
The companion package @nivaro/mcp wraps the SDK as a Model Context Protocol server, so an AI coding assistant can read and write an instance directly: collection schemas, record reads and aggregates, rehearsed creates, updates, deletes with an explicit confirm, pipeline state and transitions, and the instance's own ask-your-data assistant. It authenticates with an nvk_ API key, so role permissions, row-level security and user scopes apply unchanged; a sandbox key is read-only by construction. Install and client config snippets live in the package README (packages/mcp/README.md).
claude mcp add nivaro -e NIVARO_URL=https://nivaro.example.com -e NIVARO_TOKEN=nvk_... -- npx -y @nivaro/mcp

With recovery on, a request that meets a server that is briefly away (no answer, a 502, or a 503 with no code or DB_UNAVAILABLE / SERVER_BUSY; a 504 only for a record write) waits and tries again, up to budgetMs (default two minutes). Reads (and the read-only batch POSTs) always qualify. Creating a record (POST /items/:c), updating one or a set (PATCH /items/:c[/:id]) or deleting one (DELETE /items/:c/:id), a pipeline or workflow move, and a comment or task write qualify too: the client sends one Idempotency-Key for that write and repeats it on every try, so the server answers a lost save from its first try instead of writing twice. Other writes (bulk actions, imports, uploads, GraphQL) are never retried. Other 503 answers from the app (a list that took too long, MAINTENANCE) are answers, not outages. An error that already waited out the budget carries recoveryExhausted: true. Turn it on for every client in a page with setRecoveryDefaults({ enabled: true }); onRecoveryEvent reports waiting, then exactly one recovered or gave-up, for an outage notice. A gave-up carries the last answer’s code when it had one: IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS means the first try of that write never answered (its server may have stopped right after saving), so the change may be stored — re-read the record before trying again (the admin app does this and says so). Off by default; retry wins when both are set.
import { onRecoveryEvent, setRecoveryDefaults } from '@nivaro/sdk'

setRecoveryDefaults({ enabled: true, budgetMs: 120_000 })
onRecoveryEvent((e) => {
  if (e.type === 'waiting') showBanner(e.write ? 'Saving when the server is back…' : 'Rec…

Method | Purpose | Example / request(command) | REST operations | await nivaro.request(readItems("articles")) / graphql(query, vars?) | GraphQL queries + mutations | await nivaro.graphql(query, variables) / upload(file) | File upload | await nivaro.upload(file) / fileUrl(fileId) | Get download URL | nivaro.fileUrl("file-uuid") / setToken(token) | Set/clear auth token | nivaro.setToken("nvk_...") / getToken() | Read current token | const t = nivaro.getToken()

The SDK sends whatever token you give it as Authorization: Bearer; without one it rides the browser session cookie.
Credential | Where it comes from | Notes / Named API key nvk_… | API Keys page / createApiKey() | Scopes, expiry, IP allowlist, rate limit; sandbox keys never write. Sockets: use a ws-token. / Static user token | generateToken() / generateUserToken() | Acts as that user; also signs a socket in directly. / Session cookie | OIDC / SAML / password sign-in in the browser | No token; credentials: include. Sockets: use a ws-token. / View-as token nvm_… | An admin’s View-as | Acts as the viewed person; ends with the View-as. / OAuth access token nvo_… | Remote MCP clients (OAuth 2.1) | Accepted on /api/mcp and its tool calls only — never on other routes.

• If a static token is set, it takes priority (Authorization: Bearer header). • Otherwise, the session cookie is sent if available. • If neither exists, requests are made as unauthenticated (limits depend on public routes).
All REST operations use await nivaro.request(command). Command functions are factories that return a descriptor — no network call happens until request() executes it.

import { deleteItem } from '@nivaro/sdk'

await nivaro.request(deleteItem('articles', '123'))
Workflows are state machines that control the lifecycle of items. Each transition can be conditional, role-gated, and can trigger automations. Use these commands to read and drive workflow states.

The Pipeline Owner Matrix extends workflows with multi-dimensional ownership. It resolves which users own each workflow state based on dimensional rules (e.g., "If region=North and status=urgent, then assign to @jane").

• Owner Groups are evaluated in priority order (lower = higher priority). • Each group has filter rules (e.g., "region == North AND status == urgent"). • First group where ALL filters match assigns its users. • If no rules match, the item has no owner. • Manual Instance Owner overrides always apply (bypass rules). • Delegation via user.delegate_id also applies (temporary out-of-office reassignments).
Function | Purpose | Auth / readInstanceOwners(col, itemId) | Owners for current state | Authenticated / readStateOwners(col, itemId, stateId) | Owners for a specific state | Authenticated / readAllStateOwners(col, itemId) | Owners for all states (no N+1) | Authenticated / addInstanceOwner(col, itemId, userId, opts?) | Add manual override | Authenticated / removeInstanceOwner(ownerId) | Remove override | Authenticated / readPipelineTemplates() | List pipeline templates | Admin / readPipelineTemplate(id) | Get one template | Admin / readOwnerGroups(templateId) | Owner groups by state | Admin / readDimensions(templateId) | Matrix dimensions | Admin
The Form Schema API aggregates collection metadata, fields, groups, layouts, and relations into one normalized response. Use it to power dynamic UIs, form generators, and headless form runtimes.

Property | Type | Description / key | string | Field name (used in values/updates). / label | string | Display name. / type | string | text | number | boolean | date | select | etc. / interface | string | UI hint: text-input | textarea | toggle | date-picker. / required | boolean | If true, value must be provided. / sort | number | null | Display order within group. / hidden | boolean | If true, hidden from UI but readable via API. / validation_rules | Rule[] | Constraints: min_length, pattern, unique, etc. / visibility_rules | Rule[] | Show/hide based on other field values. / lock_condition | Rule[] | Make read-only based on field values. / computed_formula | string | null | If set, field is auto-calculated (read-only).
Command | Purpose / fetchFormSchema(collection) | Load full schema + layout + relations / evaluateFieldRules(collection, values) | Server-evaluate rules against values (no save) / readRelationOptions(collection, field, opts?) | Get picker options for a relation field / submitFormItem(collection, { mode, itemId?, values }) | Create or update via form
Form Schema uses **snake_case** (validation_rules, visibility_rules, computed_formula). The @nivaro/react package wraps these in **camelCase** (validationRules) for React — do not mix the two APIs.

@nivaro/react is a form runtime built on @nivaro/sdk. One hook (useNivaroForm) handles schema loading, field rules, visibility/lock evaluation, relation options, validation, and submit. Pair it with your own inputs (headless) or use <NivaroForm> for auto-rendering fields.

<PageRenderer slug="…" /> renders a page-builder page (widget grid) in your own app — the same surface as the admin's /p/:slug viewer: table, KPI, markdown, iframe, recent-activity, query tables (param filters, progress columns, row-click picker/drill/matrix sheets), matrix editors (inline or drawer-button), and record grids (record-grid — flat rows, or browse: true for header key pickers with roll-up totals until every key is chosen). Widget data resolves through the client identity, so permissions apply server-side. Requires NivaroProvider + a TanStack Query QueryClientProvider; supply NavigationContext to control where record links go, and an outer DrilldownContext if you host your own record sheet (PageRenderer hosts one otherwise).
import { NivaroProvider, PageRenderer } from '@nivaro/react'

<NivaroProvider client={nivaro}>
  <PageRenderer slug="budget-allocation" />
</NivaroProvider>

// Props: slug (required), hideHeader (skip the page-name row), className

These hooks work alongside useNivaroForm and require a form returned by that hook. They expose the active collection layout (tabs, sections, col_span grid, ungrouped zone position) plus field-level state, dirty tracking, and repeater management. Import all hooks from @nivaro/react.
FormSchema now includes ungroupedSort: number | null — the configured position of the Ungrouped zone relative to named groups. fetchFormSchema and useFormSchema fetch this automatically from the active layout endpoint; no extra call is needed.
Export | Kind | Purpose / LayoutForm | Component | Full layout-aware auto-renderer (tabs, sections, col_span grid, ungrouped zone). / useOrderedLayout(form) | Hook | Ordered list of groups + __ungrouped__ sentinel, reflecting ungroupedSort. / useTabState(form) | Hook | Active tab + setter + tabs list; hasTabs false when layout has no tab groups. / useSectionState(form, defaultCollapsed?) | Hook | Per-section collapse state; toggle, collapseAll, expandAll. / useFieldState(form, field) | Hook | value, error, visible, locked, required, colSpan, descriptor, onChange for one field. / useWatchFields(form, fields[]) | Hook | Reactive Record<string, unknown> slice — re-renders only when watched values change. / useFormDirty(form, initialValues?) | Hook | isDirty, dirtyFields[], isFieldDirty(field) — compares against initial or mounted values. / useFormStatus(form) | Hook | isDirty, isValid, isSubmitting, isLoading, canSubmit — one-stop status object. / useFieldArray(form, field) | Hook | append, remove, move, update, replace for ordered repeater rows.
All layout hooks read the same form object returned by useNivaroForm. They do not create extra network requests — schema and layout data are fetched once by the hook and shared.

useLiveRecord and useLiveList are react-query reads that stay current. When the host mounts a realtime adapter, other people's writes are patched into the cached data in place; without one (or while the socket reconnects) the read polls instead. Nothing to wire by hand: no socket events, no invalidation.

createSocketRealtime turns the Socket.io connection your app already holds into the adapter every live surface reads (RealtimeContext). Your app keeps owning the socket: it connects, sends auth {token} and its client:hello. The adapter joins and leaves collection rooms, admin watch rooms and live operations topics (reference counted), joins them again after every reconnect, replays missed events, and raises the same window events the admin app does (nvr:catchup-full, nvr:access-changed, nvr:config-update, nvr:force-refresh).
import { io } from 'socket.io-client'
import { createSocketRealtime, RealtimeContext } from '@nivaro/react'

const socket = io(API_URL, { transports: ['websocket', 'polling'], withCredentials: true })
socket.on('connect', async () => socket…
Shared components (My Work, Notes, tasks, record pages, collection lists, queues) read the same context, so mounting the adapter makes them live too. Set windowEvents: { forceRefresh: false } (or another key) when your app already raises that window event itself.

const { data: page, live } = useLiveList('orders', {
  filter: { status: { _eq: 'open' } },
  sort: ['-created_at'],
  fields: ['title', 'status'],
  limit: 25
})
Someone else… | What the list does / changes a row on the page | Re-reads that row as the viewer under the list's own filter and search, and patches it in place. / changes a row so it no longer matches | The re-read returns nothing, so the row leaves (a paged list refetches to fill the gap). / creates or changes a record so it now matches | Refetches the page quietly; where it belongs in the sort order is the server's to decide. / changes a sort field of a row on the page | Refetches the page (the order may have moved). / deletes a row on the page | Drops it from the cached page. / runs a bulk or raw write | Refetches the page quietly. / changes a record the filter cannot see | Nothing: an update that touches no field the filter reads cannot bring a record in.
Option | Default | Meaning / enabled | true | Pause the read and the live feed. / pollMs | 30000 | Poll interval while there is no live socket (0 = never). / safetyPollMs | none | A slow poll while the socket is live. / debounceMs | 250 | Events inside this window are handled as one patch. / includeOwn | false | Also react to this tab's own writes (a save never echoes back by default). / fields (useLiveRecord) | all | Fields to read; enables the partial re-read.
The socket only says THAT a record changed (its id, the action and the changed field names). Values always come from a fresh read through the viewer's own permission-checked /items route, so row filters, User Scopes and field policies apply exactly as on the first load. A list read always carries id (it is added to an explicit fields list) so rows can be matched to events. Changes to a related record (a filter on customer.region) do not reach a list of orders; pass safetyPollMs when that matters.
Query keys are liveRecordKey(collection, id, fields) and liveListKey(collection, query) — invalidate them yourself after a write if you set includeOwn: false and want the list re-sorted at once.

Every API answer carries an x-nivaro-request-id header — the id the slow-trace buffer, the access log and the request log share. The client puts it on NivaroError.requestId and on the onResponse hook (see Setup). A cross-origin browser call can only read it when the API exposes the header through CORS.
Call configured external APIs without exposing credentials. The SDK handles credential injection server-side. Use these commands to manage API configs, test connections, and call endpoints.
Use nivaro.graphql() to send typed GraphQL queries and mutations. The method throws on errors — no need to check response.errors manually. Uses the same auth (token/cookie) as REST.
Generate, revoke, and manage static API tokens programmatically. Tokens are prefixed with nvk_ and can have custom scopes, expiry dates, and IP allowlists.

blocks.t:
When creating a token in the admin UI, you can configure:
Setting | Description | Example / Scopes | What the token can do (read, write, admin) | ["read:all", "write:articles"] / Expires at | Expiry datetime (optional) | 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z / IP allowlist | Restrict to specific IPs (optional) | ["203.0.113.0", "203.0.113.1"] / Rate limit | Requests per minute (optional) | 100
Token values are only returned in the API response once. After you leave the page or close the dialog, the value cannot be retrieved. Copy it to a password manager or secure store immediately.
All tokens are stored as sha256 hashes in the database — the plaintext is never persisted. Use setToken() to set the SDK token at runtime.

The @nivaro/sdk command surface now covers every feature area — roughly 175 typed Command<T> factories spanning items, files, workflows, pipelines, flows, comments, webhooks, rules, custom queries, trees and hierarchies, submission forms, field watches, notification subscriptions, imports, SLA, alerts, AI endpoints (generate, summarize, validate, check-duplicates), translations, drafts, scheduled changes, record templates, saved views, API keys, widget feeds, sync jobs, ERP submissions, PDF templates, pages, queues (worklists, items, claims, saved views, trends, workload), roles & policies (RBAC/RLS), user management + out-of-office delegation, file management (list/meta/presign/transform URLs), dashboard widgets, extension item/bulk actions, throughput reporting, and more. If a REST route exists, there is a typed command for it.

Extensions are Node.js plugins that live in api/extensions/<name>/. Each exports a default object with an id and register(ctx) function. The loader auto-discovers them at startup and after "Scan for new" requests.
TypeScript (index.ts) and compiled JS (index.js) are both supported. TypeScript files load directly via tsx in dev mode.

A repair, backfill or migration an extension owns is registered with ctx.tasks.register(...) and run from the admin console at Operations → Jobs → Repair tasks (/jobs/tasks) instead of a laptop shell: a dry run reports what a real run would do and writes nothing, one run at a time per task, every run a row under Jobs with its output kept for the console, and an activity row naming who ran what and what it left behind. A task says whether it can run on THIS host (available()) — one that shells out to scripts a built image does not carry shows its CLI instead of a dead button.
ctx.tasks.register({
  key: 'my-extension:orphan-rows',
  label: 'Orphan rows',
  description: 'Removes child rows whose parent was deleted before the FK existed.',
  group: 'Data repairs',
  leaves_behind: 'zz_backup_orphans_<stamp>',
  fo…
• Routes (admin only): GET /api/ops-tasks (catalog + last ten runs each), POST /api/ops-tasks/:key/run with { "execute": true } for a real run (dry by default; 409 while one runs), GET /api/ops-tasks/runs/:id (status, progress, outcome, output tail), POST /api/ops-tasks/runs/:id/cancel (cooperative — the task checks rc.cancelled() between chunks). • The output tail lives in the process that ran the task; the run row itself is durable. • In a test, createTestContext().runTask(key, { execute }) runs the task with a recording context.

Rows of a configuration collection an extension owns the definition of — a warehouse list, a category map, a set of reference values — are checked in beside its code and registered with ctx.seeds.register(...). A seed is never applied at boot: it becomes the operational task seed:<key> whose dry run is the drift report (every row where the database differs from the file, which columns, and who last changed the row) and whose real run applies the file through the items service, as the admin who clicked, with _change_reason naming the seed. Rows match on match_by columns, never on id, so a seed survives an id-space difference between databases.
ctx.seeds.register({
  key: 'my-extension:warehouse-ordering',
  collection: 'warehouses',
  match_by: ['name'],
  rows: [
    { name: 'North DC', ordering_system: 'api' },
    { name: 'South DC', ordering_system: 'manual' }
  ],
  mode: 'f…
• fill-only creates rows the database lacks and fills columns that are empty there; a value someone set stays and is reported as drift. authoritative writes the file's values back over differing columns. • A row that matches several database rows is ambiguous: reported, never written. • GET /api/config-seeds lists the seeds; GET /api/config-seeds/:key/drift is the report as JSON (admin only). The task appears under Ops Tasks like any other.

ctx.helpVideos lets an extension ship help videos with itself. declarePage({ key, label, app }) names a page key in the registry the Videos button and the editor's Where picker use, so authors can place a video on the extension's own screens before anyone has opened them. registerStarter({ package, ids, contexts }) points at a help-video package inside the extension folder — the file Content Promotion → Help videos exports — and addContexts(videoId, contexts) adds screens (a collection, a collection at one pipeline step, or a page) to one video of it.
ctx.helpVideos.declarePage({ key: 'acme.orders.board', label: 'Orders board', app: 'admin' })
ctx.helpVideos.registerStarter({
  package: 'videos/starters.tar',             // relative to the extension folder
  contexts: [{ kind: 'page', ke…
• A starter video is imported once per database, after register() returns and in the background, as a DRAFT: never published, visible to authors only, never required viewing, rendered only when someone publishes it. An author reviews it, chooses who can watch and publishes it. • The import runs the same checks as an administrator importing the package (manifest, sizes, checksums, media probes, edits re-normalized). Screens on a collection or step this instance does not have are skipped. • A video id that already exists here is left alone, and so is one that was imported once and deleted since: each import leaves a help-video-starter-import activity row naming the video, and a later boot reads it and does nothing. • The package path must stay inside the extension folder — an absolute path, .., or a link that leads outside is refused. A bad declaration is logged and skipped; it never stops the extension loading. • Music uploaded to a starter video is dropped (an uploaded music file needs an owner); library music is kept when this instance has the track. • Self-hosted only for now: in cloud mode the declarations are recorded on the registry sheet but nothing is written. Every declaration appears on the Extensions registry sheet under Help videos; createTestContext() records them under registered.helpVideos.

An extension cannot import api/src — the API compiles with rootDir: src, and a mounted extension runs against a built image that ships no source. @nivaro/extension-kit is the contract instead: the extension context (ExtensionContext), the default export shape (ExtensionDefinition, checked by defineExtension), and every registration the context accepts — bulk and item actions, readiness and integrity checks, notes providers, mail types, digest sections, obligation kinds, signals, import processors, flow operations and triggers. The API imports its own extension contract from the same package, so the two cannot drift.
• Types are exported with export type; importing one costs nothing at runtime. • Two helpers are runtime code: hasColumn(db, table, column) — a per-database column probe for a writer that must keep working before a migration reaches the database — and requesterInsertFields / requesterSelectColumns for the ERP submission tables. • Members are only ever added to the context. An extension built against an older kit keeps compiling; a member that arrived in a later core release is documented as such on the type. • In the monorepo the kit is a workspace package; a mounted extension resolves it from the image. Released with pnpm kit:release.

nivaro ext init <id> (the CLI that ships with @nivaro/sdk) writes api/extensions/<id>/ with an index.ts on defineExtension — one setting, one hook, one scheduled job with a description, and one route behind requireAuth — a passing test on createTestContext(), and a README naming the context members it uses. The id must be kebab-case and the directory must not exist yet; --dir writes somewhere else. Restart the API and the extension appears on the Extensions page.
npx nivaro ext init acme-orders            # → api/extensions/acme-orders/
cd api && npx vitest run extensions/acme-orders
npx tsc -p extensions/tsconfig.json

A context member on its way out is listed in the kit as data — KIT_DEPRECATIONS, each entry naming the member, its replacement and the kit version it leaves in — because a @deprecated tag is invisible at runtime. The loader watches every listed member on the context it hands register(): the first use per extension per boot logs a warning, the Extensions registry sheet lists the members in use under "Deprecated members in use" with a use count, and the readiness check "Extensions avoid deprecated kit members" warns while any loaded extension still reads one. In a test, createTestContext().calls.deprecations holds one sentence per read. Nothing is deprecated today.

createTestContext() from the kit is a context whose every effect is recorded instead of sent — notifications, external calls, activity rows, flow emits, obligations — and whose registrations the test can run: runHooks(collection, action, timing, ctx), runCron(id), deliverEvent(type, payload), and invoke(method, url, req) for a route the extension registered. Its database is createTestDb({ tables }), an in-memory knex-shaped fake that covers the chain extensions use (where, whereIn, first, pluck, count, insert, update, del, raw, schema.hasColumn, transaction); joins are accepted and ignored, so seed the joined columns on the row you expect back. Nothing boots the API.
import { createTestContext } from '@nivaro/extension-kit'
import ext from './index.js'

const ctx = createTestContext({ tables: { orders: [{ id: 1, owner: 'u1' }] } })
await ext.register(ctx)
await ctx.runHooks('orders', 'create', 'after', …

Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>

A required one that is not set fails GET /api/preflight and the readiness scorecard by name, the loader logs it at boot, and the Extensions registry sheet lists every declared variable as set or not set — never its value. A long, multi-step operator script (a data conversion, a cutover chain) can be declared as a runbook. The admin Environments page lists it under Runbooks and runs it from the machine the API runs on — local development only — as a detached process, so a run that takes hours outlives the API restarting. The console shows each step, how long it took and what it said, the log tail, and offers Cancel and Resume from the step that failed.
• A real run needs a finished dry run of the same target from the last 24 hours, and the target typed back. • One runbook runs at a time on the machine. A target listed in refuse_targets is refused. • The script is started as npx tsx <script> <args> --events from the api directory, with target_env set to the target. It prints @@steps ["a","b"], then @@event {"step","status":"start|ok|fail|skip|refused","secs","lines"} per step, and ends with ### DONE — <summary> or ### FAILED at <step>: <reason>. • Resume passes resume_flag and the failed step name; the script skips the steps before it.
export default {
  id: 'my-extension',
  runbooks: [
    {
      key: 'convert',
      label: 'Data conversion',
      script: 'extensions/my-extension/scripts/convert.ts',
      dry_args: ['--dry-run'],
      go_args: ['--execute'],
      …

A runbook declared with runs_on: 'host' runs on another machine — the one that can reach what it needs (the database server, a file share). Every instance lists it, local or deployed. Starting it QUEUES the run; the host agent on that machine claims it, runs it, and streams its output back every second while the console shows the phases, the live log and an estimate.
• Install the agent on the host with cron: * * * * * bash -lc 'cd <checkout>/api && npx tsx src/scripts/runbook-agent.ts --once' (or pnpm --filter @nivaro/api run runbook:agent -- --once). Each tick checks in, then claims the oldest queued run for a runbook the extensions on that checkout declare. RUNBOOK_AGENT_HOST overrides the host name. The console says when no agent is checking in. • command (an argv starting with bash, sh, node, npx or tsx and naming a file inside the extension) runs instead of npx tsx <script>; --events is not appended. phases ([{key, label}]) draws the track before any event arrives and offers "start from phase", passed through resume_flag. • The same rules as local runbooks: a real run needs a finished dry run of the target from the last 24 hours and the target typed back; one queued or running run per runbook; Cancel takes a queued run out of the queue and stops a running one (SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL 30 seconds later). • Exit 75, or a ### REFUSED: <reason> line, records the run as refused (a lock, another job, an unreachable database) rather than done. A run whose agent stops reporting for 3 minutes reads as lost; the next tick re-attaches while the process still runs, and records its exit status (kept in a file beside the agent's lock) when it has finished. • A wrapped runbook's own step events can be printed as @@sub {…} lines: they show as the progress of the phase that is running, never as phases of their own. • Estimates: every successful phase and sub-step is timed into nivaro_runbook_step_timings. A phase's typical time is the median of its last 7 passes in the same mode; the console shows how long a full run (or a run from any phase) usually takes, and during a run the elapsed time, the current phase and sub-step, the share done, the ETA, and a stall warning when the run has been quiet longer than that phase ever was (10 minutes without history). • history_dirs ([{path, mode}], relative to the repository root) feed the estimates from runs started outside the console, such as a nightly cron: one directory per run with a summary.txt of === <n>-<phase> END … exit=0 elapsed=<m>m<s>s === lines and per phase a <n>-<phase>.log whose ─── <step> done in <m>m<ss>s ─── lines are its sub-steps. A run directory holding .nivaro-runbook-run is skipped (the console already timed it).
runbooks: [
  {
    key: 'rebuild',
    label: 'Rebuild the rehearsal database',
    runs_on: 'host',
    command: ['bash', 'extensions/my-extension/scripts/rebuild.sh', 'nightly'],
    dry_args: ['--dry'],
    go_args: [],
    resume_flag:…
